variation.original_summary: One Night Revolution is a 3-10 player hidden-ID deduction game: secret Rebels vs Informants use night look/swap powers, then day claims and discussion, then a simultaneous point to Terminate; Rebels win if an Informant is terminated.

review.evidence: No always-vote-X, always-target-X or always-claim-Rebel policy can lock a win: votes need 2+ to terminate, ties terminate all tied, framing changes Rebel results, and totals are not zero-sum. An Informant who always frames the same Rebel is eventually investigated and voted; a Rebel who always votes the same player misses 8 of 10 pairs.

Every player is Informant exactly 4 rounds and Rebel exactly 6 rounds with each partner once, so type-luck is equalized; only order is random. With scores hidden, round 9 still has ~5 candidate pairs, so investigation choice, framing, claim logic and vote reading decide points, not the draw.

Weak play can still score by lucky votes; strong play can improve by optimal investigate targets given elimination history, partner-aware framing, deceptive claims, schedule deduction, and tie-engineering votes. Not solved in 10 rounds with 4 choice steps.

Each round roles are private, Informants privately know each other, Rebel results are noisy because 'Informant' can be true or framed, and the pair schedule is hidden. Winning votes require inferring who knows what and who will vote where.
Winner follows by arithmetic: sum of stated per-round points, tie-break on Rebel points then Informant points. No referee judgment.

Turn-based text-only: private role tells, simultaneous target, simultaneous claims, simultaneous responses, simultaneous vote, public vote and terminated-role announcements. No board, no trading, no binding agreements, 10 rounds.

problems: Running announcements of total, Rebel points and Informant points let anyone read off every earlier Informant pair in all 20 matches; with each pair used once round 9 had one candidate pair left and round 10 Informants were terminated in 19 of 20.

Team survival bonus gave both Informants 2 points only if no Informant was terminated, so an Informant lost the bonus because its partner was terminated in 14 of 80 Informant rounds, punishing play it could not control.

changes.fixes: Running announcements of total, Rebel points and Informant points let anyone read off every earlier Informant pair in all 20 matches; with each pair used once round 9 had one candidate pair left and round 10 Informants were terminated in 19 of 20.
changes.what: Hide all scores until the end: announce no points during the game; announce votes and terminated roles each round only; announce every final total, Rebel points and Informant points after round 10.
changes.why: Removes the deterministic schedule leak while keeping vote and termination information for deduction; round 9 keeps ~5 candidate pairs so deception and planning stay relevant.

changes.fixes: Team survival bonus gave both Informants 2 points only if no Informant was terminated, so an Informant lost the bonus because its partner was terminated in 14 of 80 Informant rounds, punishing play it could not control.
changes.what: Individual survival bonus: each Informant who was not terminated this round gains 2 points, regardless of partner fate.
changes.why: Rewards own survival and deceptive play instead of punishing a player for a partner error; keeps Informant scoring skill-sensitive.

variation.name: One Night Revolution: Ten Nights, Hidden Ledger
variation.summary: Five players repeat 10 hidden Rebel-vs-Informant rounds on a secret pair schedule; Rebels investigate, Informants frame, all talk twice then vote to terminate, scoring hidden until the end.
variation.rules: SETUP: 5 players. Each starts with 0 total points, 0 Rebel points, 0 Informant points. Before round 1 the engine lists all 10 unordered pairs of players and shuffles the list secretly. This is the only random event. In round r (r=1 to 10) the pair in position r is the Informants; the other 3 are Rebels. Every player is Informant in exactly 4 rounds with each other player as partner exactly once, and Rebel in exactly 6 rounds. Players are told this rule but not the order. EACH ROUND, in order: 1. ROLES: Each player is privately told Rebel or Informant for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. 2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as target. A Rebel target is investigated. An Informant target is framed. An Informant may name any other player including the partner; framing a partner has no extra effect. 3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target: 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round OR at least one Informant framed that target this round, otherwise 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is always true; an 'Informant' result may be true or a frame. Informants receive no result. 4. CLAIMS (simultaneous): Every player writes one short message, e.g. claimed role, target or result. Lying allowed. All messages then shown to everyone. 5. RESPONSES (simultaneous): Every player writes one more short message. All shown to everyone. 6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes showing who voted for whom are then announced publicly. 7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise every player tied for the most votes is terminated. The round roles of terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles revealed. 8. SCORING (hidden): Each Rebel who voted for an Informant gains 2 points. If at least one terminated player is an Informant, each Rebel gains 1 more point. Each Informant gains 1 point for every Rebel who voted for a Rebel (0 to 3). Each Informant who was not terminated this round gains 2 points. Points gained while Rebel are also added to Rebel points; points gained while Informant also added to Informant points. No totals of any kind are announced during the game. Only the votes and the terminated roles are announced each round. Termination removes no one; all 5 play every round. After round 10 the engine announces every player's final total, Rebel points and Informant points and the game ends.
variation.objective: After 10 rounds the player with the highest total points wins. Tie-break: among tied, most Rebel points wins; if still tied, most Informant points wins; if still tied, draw.
variation.expected_effect: Hiding the ledger restores late-game uncertainty so Informants can still bluff and Rebels must still infer schedule, results and voting intent. Individual survival lets a good Informant profit even if its partner is caught. Talk earns its place: Rebels want to coordinate on a true Informant, Informants want Rebels to vote Rebels; interests conflict. A Rebel who just follows a proposal can lose by voting a Rebel (loses 2, gives Informants 1 each plus survival) while a correct independent vote earns 2-3.

balanced.evidence: Payoff table per round (R=Rebel, I=Informant): R votes I: +2 individual + team +1 if any I terminated (shared to all 3 R) => 2 or 3. R votes R: +0 + team 0/1 => 0 or 1. So voting believed-I dominates voting believed-R by +2 whatever termination does. I: +1 per R voting R (0-3 shared to both I) +2 if self not terminated else 0. I vote does not score directly, only affects termination/survival. No unconditional dominance because R does not know who is I: 'Rebel' result always true clearance, 'Informant' result = true I OR framed Rebel. Framing choice has no dominant target ex ante. Thoughtless policies: (a) always target/vote P1: as R in 6 rounds, P1 is I in ~4/10 rounds? Actually each pair appears once: P1 is I with T in 1/4 I-rounds and I without T in others. Blind vote hits I ~40% vs sensible ~>60-70% using clearances + talk, so loses 2pts in ~2+ rounds = -4 to -6 total; as I, blind vote does not create misvotes and draws attention, increasing termination risk losing +2 survival. Tested vs sensible (investigate+share true results+coordinate on non-cleared) and vs random: blind does not win/draw almost every time, it trails. (b) always vote cycle to force 1-1-1-1-1 zero-termination: R then forgo +2/+1, I forgo survival risk but also forgo misvote points if R coordinate; sensible R deviating to concentrate votes gets +3 while cooperator gets 0/1, so cycle not never-loses. WINNER RULE (highest total after 10, tie-break R-points then I-points): no policy guarantees >= all others; symmetry gives all seats ex ante 6R+4I rounds, all simultaneous choices, no move-order/info edge. All 5 can realistically finish first via better deduction/deception. No labelled PD-type ordering to falsify.

playable.evidence: Complete/unambiguous: setup pair-list shuffle, r=1..10 pair=I rest=R, ROLES private + partner to I, NIGHT simultaneous target other, RESULTS rule for R only, CLAIMS simultaneous short message then show, RESPONSES simultaneous then show, VOTE simultaneous for other then publish who-for-whom, TERMINATION <2 votes=>none else plurality-tie terminated + only terminated roles revealed, SCORING hidden formula + accumulation to total/R-points/I-points, termination removes no one, final totals announced. Finite 10 rounds, arithmetic winner highest total with arithmetic tie-breaks. No judge/board/clock needed. Capabilities used: private_values, simultaneous_choice, free_text_talk, fixed_rounds are supported; conditional scoring 'if any I terminated +1' and plurality termination are single-step when/if + calc workaround, allowed. Limits: claimed attributes 6, choice_steps 4 (NIGHT,CLAIMS,RESPONSES,VOTE), hidden 3 (roles+partner, investigation results, hidden scores; pair order is pre-game random not per-round), random_draws_per_round 0 (sole shuffle pre-round1), rounds 10, steps 9 => all <=20/4/20/3/1/40. 5-player talk: present where disagreement exists (R want to coordinate on I, I want to induce R-R votes; following wrong proposal costs 2pts/survival), simultaneous write-then-show not sequential, round correctly opens with private info not empty talk. Fixed-length total game: cooperation (R coordinating) still pays +2+1 in late rounds; no safe defect that wins every late round.

reasoning_over_luck.evidence: Chance ~0-5%: only random event is secret shuffle of 10 pairs pre-game; per-round investigation/framing/votes/talk have no dice. Role counts equalized by design (each player I 4x with each partner once, R 6x), so shuffle changes order only, not totals. If all follow intended good strategy (R investigate truthfully, use true 'Rebel' clearances, coordinate votes; I concentrate frames on Rebels, lie, push R-R votes): per-round outcome depends on target choices, message persuasion, vote coordination, not on draw; symmetric perfect play => tied totals => draw, not random winner. Good play overcomes deal: R reasoning about clearances vs possibly-framed 'Informant', tracking remaining pairs (e.g., past partners cannot re-pair), modelling who frames/claims; I reasoning about which Rebel to frame and what lie survives. Skilled > unskilled clearly: skilled R gains +2 vs 0 per round, skilled I gains +1 per misled R +2 survival vs 0. Inference target exists and actionable via target/claim/vote.

triage.reason: With votes 3,3,4,1,1 seats 1 and 3 have 2 votes each for the most, so per R14 they must be terminated, not seat 4; the tests expect the opposite 0-indexed mapping and a 0 informant count.
triage.guidance: Fix vote-count expectations to 1-indexed seat numbers: expect is_terminated True for seats 1 and 3, False for others, and compute terminated_informant_count from the actual round-r Informant pair. For R22 test continued play by offering next-round choices to all 5, not by asserting stale is_terminated/count values.
